eips.title: Frame Transaction
eips.summary: Frame Transaction spec PRs, DevNet readiness, gas accounting interaction with multidimensional fees, and tooling gaps were discussed throughout the call.

moments.context: Marc noted 13 open PRs against EIP-8141 and asked whether any need attention before Frames DevNet Zero launches.
Discussion of Frames DevNet Zero launch timing, with clients Geth, Ethrex, and Nethermind ready; waiting on PandaOps availability.
Anders presented how Frame Transactions interact with multidimensional fee markets, noting frames aim to be an enduring format that should harmonize with future fee designs.
Viem maintainer feedback relayed: JSON-RPC for frame transactions feels underspecified, needing gas estimation and simulation support.
Mislav described building an 8130 implementation on top of 8141 and integrating additional standards for wallet and app developer tooling.

eips.title: Keystore Accounts
eips.summary: Discussed as the keystore accounts standard being built on top of frames, with harmonization efforts and compatibility with ERC-8403.

moments.context: Daniil mentioned a PR to make frames compatible with ERC-8403 and EIP-8130 for keystore reading.
Chris from Base said they are interested in unified max fee for the 8130 transaction type but want parity with frames.
Mislav presented Ethlabs' effort to build an 8130 implementation on top of 8141 with additional developer tooling standards.

eips.summary: Discussed as a key management ERC for keystore compatibility with frames and EIP-8130.

moments.context: Daniil mentioned a PR to enable frames to read the keystore, making them compatible with ERC-8403 and EIP-8130.
Daniil asked Mislav whether ERC-8403 was considered for key management; Mislav said he would include it and provide feedback.

eips.title: State Creation Gas Cost Increase
eips.summary: Discussed in the context of state gas metering and how a multidimensional fee market would likely remove its reservoir design.

moments.context: Anders noted that EIP-8037 adds its own metering to state, which a multidimensional fee market would extend with separate base fees.
Anders said that most multidimensional fee market designs under consideration would remove the 8037 reservoir design.
Maria noted the reservoir from 8037 would still be needed for legacy transactions that lack separate gas limits.

eips.title: Unified multidimensional fee market
eips.summary: Presented by Anders as the unified multidimensional fee market proposal providing a single fungible max fee across resources.

moments.context: Anders explained EIP-7999's single max fee concept, which prevents transaction failure when one resource's base fee drifts above its individual cap.

eips.title: Fee market change for ETH 1.0 chain
eips.summary: Chris from Base referenced it when noting that L2 multi-dimensional fees today exist under the 1559 model as a hidden fee.

moments.context: Chris clarified that the hidden L1 data fee on L2 exists under the current 1559 fee structure.

eips.title: Transaction Assertions via State Diff Opcode
eips.summary: Highlighted as enabling transaction assertions via state diff opcode, important for clear signing and hardware wallet security.

moments.context: Mislav listed EIP-7906 as a key standard to integrate, noting it enables wallets to simulate state changes and encode post-transaction assertions.
Mislav described a mock UI demo where a wallet encodes a transaction assertion with 7906, enabling clear-signed review on hardware wallets.

eips.summary: Mislav proposed adapting EIP-7715 to work with the 8130 sessions system as part of the harmonization effort.

moments.context: Mislav said the idea is to adapt 7715 and 7710 to work with 8130's sessions system, noting he tested the Solidity implementation.

eips.summary: Mislav mentioned adapting EIP-7710 alongside 7715 to work with the 8130 sessions system.

moments.context: Mislav listed 7710 as a standard to adapt for compatibility with 8130 sessions within the harmonization effort.

eips.title: Wallet Call API
eips.summary: Mislav mentioned exploring whether the Wallet Call API can be extended to support frame transaction expressiveness.

moments.context: Mislav said they want to explore whether EIP-5792 wallet call API can be extended for batches and new features, or if a new standard is needed.

eips.summary: Listed by Mislav among other account-abstraction efforts the harmonization work has to stay compatible with.

moments.context: Mislav mentioned 4337 alongside 7702 as other relevant efforts in the broader frames and account abstraction landscape.
